label: Tangent Vectors
notes: This chapter, printed pages 50 to 76, builds the tangent space without leaning on an ambient space. We will pass freely between three viewpoints: a derivation acting on functions, a velocity of a curve, and a tuple of coordinate components. Keep all three in mind, because each one makes a different computation easy.

label: From Arrows to Operators
notes: In Euclidean space an arrow at a point is also a directional-derivative operator. That operator is what survives onto a manifold. Stress that the base point is part of the data: the same components at a different point give a different operator, because differentiation happens at the attachment point, not in the air.

label: Derivations at a Point
notes: Define a tangent vector as a linear map on smooth germs satisfying the Leibniz rule at p. Show that linearity plus Leibniz forces it to annihilate constants. The product rule is the load-bearing axiom; everything coordinate-free about tangent vectors descends from these two lines, so spend real time here.

label: The Coordinate Basis
notes: A chart turns the abstract derivation space into components. The coordinate vectors are the pullbacks of the standard partials under the chart. Emphasize dimension: the tangent space has the same dimension as the manifold, and these n vectors form a basis. The sphere picture audits the formula, it is not the definition.

label: Coordinate Components
notes: Every tangent vector expands in the coordinate basis with components given by its action on the coordinate functions. This is the bridge between the abstract derivation and a computable n-tuple. Warn students that the n-tuple is not intrinsic: it belongs to a chart, and a different chart gives a different tuple for the same vector.

label: The Differential
notes: The differential, or pushforward, of a smooth map sends tangent vectors at p to tangent vectors at F(p). The defining formula is dF_p(v) acting on h equals v acting on h composed with F. It is coordinate-free by construction. Make sure students see that the pullback of the test function is what makes this well defined.

label: The Jacobian Matrix
notes: Once charts are fixed on both sides, the differential becomes a matrix: the Jacobian of the coordinate representative. Walk through the curve picture. The velocity of the image curve equals the Jacobian times the domain velocity. This is the concrete payoff of the abstract definition, and it is exactly what the notebook checks symbolically.

label: The Chain Rule
notes: Functoriality is the chain rule in categorical clothing. The differential of a composite is the composite of differentials, and the identity map pushes forward to the identity. In coordinates this is just matrix multiplication of Jacobians. Tell students this single law reorganizes a whole semester of multivariable calculus into one clean statement.

label: Change of Coordinates
notes: Components transform by the transition Jacobian, never by copying the same tuple. Polar coordinates make this vivid: the angular basis vector has length r and the chart dies at the origin. The applied lab sweeps r and shows the naive copy law accumulating error while the correct law has zero residual.

label: Velocity of a Curve
notes: A curve produces a tangent vector by differentiating test functions along it. Conversely every tangent vector is some curve's velocity, so the derivation and velocity pictures coincide. At a boundary point the curve domain matters: two-sided curves force zero normal velocity, while one-sided endpoint curves realize inward and outward vectors.

label: The Tangent Bundle
notes: Collect all tangent spaces into one set, the tangent bundle, a smooth 2n-manifold. Its charts pair base coordinates with velocity coordinates, so locally it is a product. The projection forgets the velocity and returns the base point. Stress that local product structure does not force a global product; that gap is the seed of bundle theory.

label: Alternative Definitions
notes: The chapter compares the derivation, velocity, and equivalence-class definitions. They all describe the same object but at different costs: derivations are clean for proofs, velocities are intuitive, and physicist tuples are fast to compute but chart-bound. Encourage students to switch viewpoints fluidly rather than committing to one.

label: Recap
notes: Recap the through-line: a tangent vector is attached to a point and differentiates functions there. The differential is its pushforward, the Jacobian is its matrix once charts are chosen, components obey a transition law, and the tangent bundle packages everything functorially. These invariants are exactly the executable checks in the notebook.
